annotationRationale: Both routes use positional place values and valid digit ranges. The main route eliminates a shared expression and factors a quadratic; the alternative uses integer bounds to determine the base.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The statement and choices are consistent. Independently, positional expansion gives d=2 and n=9, so n+d=11, choice B. No figure or grading conflict is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: Both useful accessible routes are supplied: eliminate the shared place values, or bound the integer base. The references' different quadratic-solving endings do not require additional methods.
review.annotationCheck: cnm_024 appropriately identifies the assessed numeral-system concept. Linear solving, quadratic factoring, and integer bounds are correctly distinguished at method level.
review.areaCheck: Number Theory is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Subtracting the expansions gives 4-d=6d-10, hence d=2. The resulting quadratic factors correctly as (n-9)(3n+29)=0. Positivity excludes the second root; n=9 makes every digit valid and gives 11.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited third-party sources support the argument: LIVE supplies elimination, and AoPS Solution 3 supplies the displayed quadratic factorization. AoPS Solution 1 instead uses the quadratic formula. The source-informed-original designation is appropriate, with sufficiently independent explanatory prose.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The opening explains why subtraction fits. Place values, elimination, factoring, root selection, and digit validity are all reconstructible by an AMC 10 learner.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All three immediate IDs are supported: cnm_024 for positional expansion, cnm_042 for solving the linear equation in d, and cnm_224 for quadratic factoring and the zero-product rule.

A-SSE.B.3a provides only partial overlap because function zeros are not discussed. cnm_024 has no supplied US link.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The base-six digit gives 0≤d≤5. For positive n≤8 the first value is at most 213; for n≥10 it is at least 320. Thus n=9 and d=2. Both sides of the second condition equal 265, confirming the solution.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 2 supplies the base-estimation idea. Replacing its trial and error with complete bounds is a substantive original explanation, correctly labeled source-informed-original.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The digit restrictions motivate the bounds, both excluded ranges include their endpoints, and the unused condition is explicitly verified.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_024 covers the expansions and digit restrictions. math:integer-diophantine-equations precisely covers using finite bounds and integrality to prove completeness.
